questions.stem: Which of the following is not seen in the structure of Mucormycosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Beta 1, 3D glucan
  • Invasive fungal infections (fungal infection of an otherwise sterile site, such as the bloodstream or deep tissues) are associated with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in situations where diagnosis and initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy is delayed.
  • The gold standard remains histopathologic examination of biopsy material from affected tissues alongside culture. Routine fungal culture can be helpful, however results may also be confounding.  Sensitivity of culture is generally low and is largely dependent on the quality of the specimen submitted.  Also, some fungal pathogens require prolonged incubation, which can further delay diagnosis.
  • Because of these limitations, alternative diagnostic assays for detection of IFIs, including both molecular testing and identification of fungal biomarkers, including detection of the pan-fungal biomarker 1-3 beta-d-glucan or BDG are very useful for timely detection.

Beta 1, 3 glycan is a component of the cell wall of most of the fungi except in some organisms (organisms lack BDG or produce it in low amounts)

  • Mucormycosis / Zygomycetes
  • Cryptococcus
  • Blastomycosis

Results from this assay need to be used in conjunction with the other diagnostic procedures previously mentioned, including imaging studies, culture and histopathologic examination of biopsy material as available.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:724t, 726t, 732

Toxoplasma gondii

Option D: The given image shows the life cycle of toxoplasma gondii

Life cycle of T. gondi

  • Definitive host – Cats (enteric cycle)
  • Intermediate hosts – humans, mice, rats etc. (exo enteric cycle)
  • Both asexual reproduction and sexual reproduction occurs within the mucosal epithelium of the small intestine of cats
  • Tachyzoites and tissue cyst represents stages of asexual reproduction
  • Oocysts are formed by sexual reproduction
  • In definitive hosts – all three forms Tachyzoites, tissue cysts and Oocysts occur. In intermediate host only Tachyzoites and tissue cysts are present

Asexual stage

  • Oocysts (containing sporozoites) or tissue cysts (containing bradyzoites) are ingested by intermediate hosts 🡪 Bradyzoites and sporozoites are released in the intestinal epithelium to form Tachyzoites 🡪Divides and replicates in all the mammalian cells except RBCs🡪 Tissue cysts are formed
  • Sexual stage – Occurs in cat (definitive host) and Oocysts are formed which after sporulation are excreted

questions.stemHtml: A man with FUO presented to the hospital. He travels frequently around the world for his job. The bone marrow picture is shown below. Which of the following investigations is most appropriate for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
rK39 for leishmaniasis
  • Option A: The history of frequent travel and fever of unknown origin suggests infectious cause. The image of bone marrow biopsy shows Donovan bodies (LD bodies) indicating leishmaniasis. It can be diagnosed by rK39 antigen test
  • In humans, the disease present in 4 different forms
  1. Visceral leishmaniasis / kala azar
  2. Cutaneous leishmaniasis
  3. Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis
  4. Diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis

questions.stem: Which of the following causes aplastic crisis in hereditary spherocytosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Parvovirus
  • Option D: Parvovirus is a non-enveloped, single stranded DNA virus.
  • Aplastic crisis in a child with hereditary spherocytosis is most likely due to infection of Parvovirus.
  • This aplastic crisis is due to the transient arrest of erythropoiesis where the Parvovirus infects and kills red cell precursors. Patient with aplastic crisis appears ill with fever, malaise and pale with tachycardia and tachypnoea due to profound anemia.

questions.stemHtml: A stool sample is collected and processed for examination. Identify the level at which parasite ova will be seen when viewed under microscope.
questions.solutionHtml:
D
  • Option D: The image shows formaline ether sedimentation technique for stool concentration. sediment at the bottom (D) part of the tube contains the eggs and cysts of parasites.

questions.stemHtml: A 27 years old male presented with fever, dyspnoea, palpitations and tachycardia. The echocardiography revealed vegetation in the septal leaflets. Tissue sections from them reveal the following findings as shown in the image. What is likely the Diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Acute angle branching septate hyphae- Aspergillus

options.label: C
options.text: Right angled branching septate hyphae – Fusarium

options.label: D
options.text: Pigmented septate hyphae at 90 degrees – mucormycosis

questions.answerText: Acute angle branching septate hyphae- Aspergillus
questions.solutionHtml:
Acute angle branching septate hyphae- Aspergillus
  • Option A: The image shows fungal hyphae of Aspergillus species with non-pigmented, narrow, septate hyphae branching at acute angle
  • Invasive aspergillosis is an opportunistic infection seen in immunocompromised individuals. Rhinocerebral Aspergillus infection in immunocompromised individuals resembles that caused by mucormycosis.

questions.stemHtml: An emergency surgery was conducted for intestinal obstruction and segment of the intestine resected with worms embedded in mucosa as shown in the image. Which of the following is correct regarding the pathogen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Esophageal distal end bulb
  • Option D: The given image shows Ascaris lumbricoides. The distal end of the esophagus is globular known as esophageal bulb.
  • Ascaris is the most common human helminths and distributed worldwide.
  • Adult worms live in the small intestine (85% in the jejunum and 15% in the ileum)
  • The adult worms are large cylindrical worms with tapering ends, the anterior end being more pointed than the posterior.

questions.stemHtml: A patient presented with meningitis and the CSF sample was subjected to gram staining and microscopy and appears as shown below. Which of the following features/tests will be characteristic of the organism?

options.label: A
options.text: Oxidase and catalase negative, does not ferment inulin

options.label: B
options.text: Ferment glucose and maltose but not inulin

options.label: C
options.text: Oxidase and catalase are positive and do not ferment maltose or glucose.

questions.solutionHtml:
Catalase negative, optochin sensitive
  • Option D: The given clinical features of meningitis and the slide showing gram negative diplococci suggests streptococcus pneumonia.
  • It is catalase negative and optochin sensitive and ferments inulin.
  • Pneumonia are the commensals in upper respiratory tract and can cause pneumonia, sinusitis, otitis media, bronchitis, bacteraemia, meningitis, peritonitis and other infectious processes.

questions.stemHtml: A 32 years old construction worker came to the hospital with complaints of cough, fever and hemoptysis. The sputum smear examination done shows the following image. What is the sequence of staining?

options.label: B
options.text: Carbol fuschin – acid alcohol - Methylene blue

options.label: C
options.text: Methylene blue – malachite green – acetic acid – water

questions.answerText: Carbol fuschin – acid alcohol - Methylene blue
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbol fuschin – acid alcohol - Methylene blue
  • Option B: The given clinical features and the image suggests diagnosis of tuberculosis.
  • The image shows ZN staining. Tuberculous bacilli appears bright red against blue background.

Steps in ZN staining are

  1. Place the sample on the slide and evenly spread by rotational movements
  2. Air dry and fix it by passing over flame
  3. Apply Carbol fuschin and heat to fix it
  4. Wash with water to remove excess stain
  5. Decolorize with alcohol
  6. Apply Methylene blue/malachite green stain
  7. Wash with water and remove excess stain
  8. Visualize under microscope

questions.stemHtml: A 45 years old man developed generalized muscle spasm and arching backwards as shown in the image. He had sustained a puncture wound on his leg a few days back. What is the mechanism of action of the toxin responsible for this abnormal posturing?

options.label: A
options.text: Presynaptic inhibition of Acetyl choline receptors

options.label: B
options.text: Presynaptic inhibition of GABA and glycine release

options.label: C
options.text: Cleavage of SNARE proteins, preventing Acetyl choline release

questions.answerText: Presynaptic inhibition of GABA and glycine release
questions.solutionHtml:
Presynaptic inhibition of GABA and glycine release
Explanation for incorrect options:-
  • Option B: The image shows backward bending (opisthotonus) position of the person and the history of puncture wound few days back suggests diagnosis of tetanus.
  • Tetanospasmin is the toxin responsible for this. It acts by causing presynaptic inhibition of GABA and Glycine release.
  • The incubation period of C. tetani ranges from 4 – 5 days up to 3 weeks. Muscle spasms usually involve the area of injury first and then muscles of jaw causing trismus or lockjaw. Gradually, other voluntary muscles involved, you resulting in tonic spasms.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:724t, 726t, 732
